premises: Temkin, arXiv:0904.1592v2, Theorem 1.2.1: every Noetherian quasi-excellent generically reduced scheme X over Spec Q admits a finite blowup sequence with regular centers disjoint from the preimages of X_reg and with regular final scheme.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, conventions and §§2–4: over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, a variety may be reduced and nonnormal. On a reduced projective variety, canonical evaluation gives |s|≤1 for global sections, and a generating section system has maximum canonical norm one at every analytic point. Rational PL functions are uniformly dense in C0. For an actual ample rational L, Hdom(c1(L))⊂H(L); every genuine L-psh potential is a decreasing net limit in Hdom(c1(L)), and every continuous genuine L-psh potential is a uniform limit on that same actual bundle. Genuine psh cones admit constants in nef classes, finite maxima in one class, positive sums with corresponding class sums, and decreasing varying-class limits whenever the limit is generically finite. Dominant pullback between integral projective varieties preserves genuine psh potentials. Nef potentials admit decreasing finite rational Fubini–Study approximants in ample classes approaching the nef class. These approximation and closure assertions require no envelope property.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Proposition 4.12, Theorem 4.22, Corollary 4.23 and Proposition 4.28: on a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, genuine psh potentials are finite on divisorial valuations and uniquely determined there. For genuine ϕ and usc ψ, inequality on divisorial valuations implies inequality everywhere. The topology of divisorial pointwise convergence is Hausdorff, and ϕ↦sup(ϕ−f) is continuous for fixed real PL f. On an irreducible variety, sup ϕ equals its generic trivial-valuation value.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 5.11, Lemmas 5.13 and 5.17, Theorem 5.20 and Corollary 5.21: on an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, a numerical class has the envelope property exactly when its sup-normalized genuine psh space is compact in the divisorial topology. For an ample class, EP is equivalent to continuity of envelopes of all continuous obstacles; envelopes obey the uniform Lipschitz inequality. On a smooth connected projective variety every nef class has EP and normalized compactness. If π:Y→X is birational and θ is approached by target classes θ_m having EP with θ_m−θ ample, genuine pullback PSH(X,θ)→PSH(Y,π*θ) is an onto homeomorphism.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorems 7.1, 7.8, 7.14 and 7.18 and Propositions 7.2, 7.7, 7.19 and 7.21: on a reduced projective variety X of dimension n over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, the intersection energy pairing for ample psh entries extends uniquely as a symmetric increasing usc pairing into R∪{−∞}, continuous along genuine decreasing nets. E_ω(ϕ)=(ω,ϕ)^(n+1)/((n+1)(ω^n)) is concave, increasing, usc and decreasing-net continuous. Its finite-energy cone contains bounded psh potentials, is convex and upward closed within PSH, and has finite mixed pairings. Differences of finite-energy potentials on the linear-growth locus admit the compatible signed multilinear pairing. Mixed products of ample genuine finite-energy entries are positive Radon measures of raw mass (ω_1⋯ω_n). On relatively integrally closed test configurations retaining the original generic fiber, their PL formula has coefficients ord_E(X_0)·((ω_1,X+D_1)|E⋯(ω_n,X+D_n)|E). Mixed measures converge weakly along genuine decreasing nets with finite-energy endpoints. Genuine finite-energy tests are integrable against finite-energy mixed measures. More generally, an integrable psh test ϕ_0 and decreasing psh approximants to all entries satisfy ϕ_0j μ_j→ϕ_0 μ weakly; its integral is the test-containing pairing minus the zero-test pairing. Energy pairings and raw mixed measures are compatible with normalization pullback and pushforward for pulled genuine potentials, without requiring onto pullback.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Proposition 8.3, Theorem 8.5 and Corollary 8.6: on a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field with ample ω, the outer energy E↓, defined using continuous majorants, is increasing, concave, translation equivariant, agrees with E on genuine psh potentials, and is continuous along decreasing upper-bounded usc nets. Under EP it equals E(P(u)) for upper-bounded usc u whenever the envelope is genuine. For fixed real PL f and every ϕ∈E1(ω), E↓(ϕ+tf)=E(ϕ)+t∫f MA_ω(ϕ)+O_f(t²), with the error constant uniform in ϕ. For every continuous f the two-sided derivative at zero is ∫f MA_ω(ϕ). Here MA_ω is probability normalized.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, §§7.4, 9 and Proposition 11.1: let X be irreducible projective of positive dimension over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and ω ample. For a Radon probability measure μ, E∨(μ)=sup_{ϕ∈E1}(E(ϕ)−∫ϕ μ) is finite exactly when every genuine E1 potential is μ-integrable. Put J(ϕ)=sup ϕ−E(ϕ), D=E∨(μ), and J_μ(ϕ)=D−E(ϕ)+∫ϕ μ. For finite D, J(ϕ)≤C_n(J_μ(ϕ)+D). Maximizing genuine E1 nets have MA measures converging weakly to μ. Weak convergence of genuine psh potentials with eventually bounded J implies L1(μ) convergence for every finite-dual-energy μ. The energy inequalities give I≥0, I–J comparability, strict concavity and J(tϕ)≤C_n t²J(ϕ) for normalized ϕ and 0≤t≤1. Every divisorial Dirac measure has finite dual energy. These assertions do not assume EP or inverse-equation existence.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorems 7.40 and 7.44, Corollary 7.41 and Corollaries 10.4–10.6: on an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field with ample ω, genuine E1 potentials satisfy strict-winning locality 1_{ϕ>ψ}MA(max(ϕ,ψ))=1_{ϕ>ψ}MA(ϕ) and comparison ∫_{ϕ<ψ}MA(ψ)≤∫_{ϕ<ψ}MA(ϕ). Mixed finite-energy products agree on an open set where their corresponding potentials agree. Equality of MA measures is equivalent to I(ϕ,ψ)=0 and to ϕ−ψ being one real constant. If a∈PSH(ω), b∈E1(ω), and a≤b almost everywhere for MA(b), then a≤b everywhere. These statements require no EP.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 12.8 and Theorem 13.1: let X be irreducible projective over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and ω ample. If ω has EP, the genuine finite-energy MA operator is onto all Radon probability measures of finite intrinsic dual energy, and the dual supremum for each such measure is attained by an actual genuine E1 potential. For every continuous obstacle f, p=P_ω(f) is continuous genuine psh and satisfies ∫(f−p) MA_ω(p)=0. No smoothness or support hypothesis is imposed on X or the finite-energy target.

Boucksom–Eriksson, arXiv:1805.01016v3, Theorem 7.14, Proposition 8.3, Theorem 8.4, Proposition 8.5 and Theorem 8.18: on a geometrically reduced projective scheme over any complete non-Archimedean field, including a trivially valued field, psh metrics on actual semiample rational line bundles admit decreasing smooth semipositive regularization; for continuous metrics the convergence is uniform. Mixed measures of smooth semipositive metrics are positive Radon measures defined with the analytic fundamental cycle and have raw intersection mass. They commute by pushforward with every complete-field extension. They extend uniquely to continuous psh-regularizable metrics by uniform-to-weak continuity, retaining positivity, symmetry, multilinearity and raw intersection mass. For model metrics on fixed actual bundles on a flat projective model, the metric on their Deligne pairing is the corresponding model Deligne-pairing metric. BJ Remark 7.23 identifies the resulting continuous mixed operator with its intersection-energy operator.
